episodes.title: Are microplastics harming us?
episodes.description: How much plastic do you use on a daily basis? And how much of it is used to package or prepare food? Recently, scientists are becoming increasingly concerned that microplastics, tiny bits of plastic invisible to the naked eye, are entering our bodies through these food sources... but it is unclear exactly what the long-term health effects will be. Becca and Phil discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. 6 Minute English now has a VIDEO VERSION! It's the same programme that you know and lo…

episodes.title: Learning from different generations
episodes.description: When you were younger, did you have a special bond with your grandparents? Many of us develop particularly close attachments with older family members, but did you know that this ability for the oldest and youngest of our society to get along in a friendly way is not limited to families? In fact, there are some projects which pair together nurseries and retirement homes, to help reduce feelings of loneliness and improve everybody's general health and happiness. Georgie and Phil discuss this and…

episodes.title: Could vaccines cure cancer?
episodes.description: When was the last time you had a vaccination, and what was it for? Many of us get vaccinations when we are children or when we go travelling, but did you know that scientists have been developing vaccines that can be personalised to help your body keep itself clear of some specific cancer types? Georgie and Phil discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. 6 Minute English now has a VIDEO VERSION! 6 Minute English now comes with a video! It's the same programme that you know and love, but no…

episodes.title: Is aircon the answer to a heating world?
episodes.description: Do you ever feel it is too hot to sleep? With climate change gradually increasing world temperatures, people across the world are becoming increasingly affected by hot weather. In many locations, air conditioning is used to help cool down homes and workplaces, but not everyone has access to this. And it isn't just about getting a good night's sleep – extremely hot weather can be a serious health risk. Georgie and Neil discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. 6 Minute English now has a VI…

episodes.title: What should you eat for a better night’s sleep?
episodes.description: Have you ever had the feeling of lying awake at night, unable to get to sleep? Many of us know what it is like to struggle with sleep, especially if we have drunk too much tea or coffee before bed! But did you know that your sleep quality can be affected by other parts of your diet too? Georgie and Phil discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. Get a free transcript and quiz at bbclearningenglish.com (currently experiencing technical issues). Sign up for our email newsletter for tips and…

episodes.title: Why has gold got so expensive?
episodes.description: Many of us own jewellery or other items that are gold coloured, but do you own anything that is made from real gold? Gold is a precious metal, which means that there is a limited supply in the world. This not only makes it expensive, but also means that it holds a relatively stable value. So, why are investors interested in it, and should the rest of us start buying more of it? Georgie and Phil discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. 6 Minute English now has a VIDEO VERSION! 6 Minute En…

episodes.title: Are people drinking less alcohol?
episodes.description: In recent generations many people have chosen to stop drinking alcohol. Surveys from the UK suggest that 16 to 24-year-olds are more likely to be non-drinkers than the older generations. Many people are sharing their experience of drinking less alcohol or being completely sober on social media. Some people have been saying that they want to go out more to drink and have fun with friends, but they have concerns about fitness and wellness. Georgie and Neil discuss this and teach you some new voca…

episodes.title: Why does heartbreak hurt so much?
episodes.description: Anyone who has had their heart broken will know how horrible it feels. But did you know that the pain you feel is not just imaginary – it registers in the same part of the brain that processes physical pain. So, why do we feel this pain? And if it feels so bad, what is the point of being in love in the first place? Neil and Georgie discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. 6 Minute English now has a VIDEO VERSION! 6 Minute English now comes with a video! It's the same programme that you k…

episodes.title: The Global Story: AI can imitate a human. But can it think like one?
episodes.description: For decades, computer scientists have been trying to figure out whether computers can think. But with the advent of highly sophisticated chatbots like Claude and ChatGPT…might we finally have our answer? This week we’re introducing The Global Backstory, the new strand of our show that explores the history behind the news today. We constantly hear stories about artificial intelligence, but most of them are about where AI is going; in this five-episode series we’re looking at where it came from.…

episodes.title: Deadlock at UN climate summit in Turkey
episodes.description: The COP31 summit has gone into a second day of overtime after talks were suspended for the night. There is no agreement in sight with the European Union and Pacific Island nations threatening to walk away without agreeing to a deal because the draft text makes no mention of reducing global demand for fossil fuels. Also: Croatians take to the streets over the death in hospital of a psychiatric patient who was beaten and smothered. We hear from British endurance athlete Lewis Pugh who swam throug…

episodes.title: The Happy Pod: The 'amazing’ device that controls Tourette's
episodes.description: We meet 17-year-old Mylo who's taken part in a trial of the watch-like device that suppresses his Tourette's tics. He can even now go to the cinema without fear of causing a disturbance by constantly moving or clearing his throat. Also: the chef in Japan who's known poverty and illness and now offers free meals to people in the position he was once in; the NASA spacecraft, Voyager One, that's become the first human-made object to reach a point one light day from Earth; the surf school in Senega…

episodes.title: Man found guilty of starting deadly LA wildfire
episodes.description: Jonathan Rinderknecht is found guilty of starting the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles, which displaced thousands of people and became one of the most destructive fires in the city’s history. Also: Donald Trump describes his relationship with the leaders of Russia and China as “fantastic”, after meeting with them in Shenzhen. The US president also threatens a ban on American firms building AI data centres overseas, saying they must stay in the US. Russian drones continue to attack Ukraine,…

episodes.title: UK agrees deal on closer cooperation with EU
episodes.description: UK and EU agree new deal covering food exports, youth mobility and carbon emissions. European Commission President, Ursula von der Leyen, said it marked a "turning point" in relations. Also: BBC speaks to people inside the besieged city of Taiz in Yemen. Why the Malaysian government wants to settle 10,000 Rohingyas in Turkey. A group of eight European and developing countries at the UN climate summit in Turkey says a global call to "accelerate the phase-out of fossil fuels" must be restored to…

episodes.title: Abusers convicted in Joanne Young case echoing Pelicot
episodes.description: In the first trial of its kind in England, four men have been convicted of raping and sexually abusing a British woman, in a harrowing case that bears similarities to that of Gisèle Pelicot in France. Like Pelicot, Joanne Young chose to allow her name to be made public, after discovering that her then-husband had advertised her online to strangers for sex, repeatedly drugged her and raped her. British police sought the expertise of French investigators on the Pelicot case to assist them in brin…

episodes.title: UN court says Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingyas
episodes.description: The International Court of Justice finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority. It's the first such ruling against a state by the court. The ICJ rejected Myanmar’s argument that it had responded to insurgent attacks. Also: the presidents of China, the US and Russia stress the importance of stable energy flows, UN reform and the prevention of nuclear proliferation at a trilateral summit, internet access is cut in South Korean exam halls, amid fears of cheating. And a re…

episodes.title: BBC reports from Ukraine's undergound frontier
episodes.description: We go inside the old Soviet-era gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia. The BBC is the first international broadcaster to enter the tunnels where this subterranean battle is taking place. Also: the AI giant Anthropic is set to raise more than 80 billion dollars in its initial public offering, breaking a record set by SpaceX. President Trump pushes back against global regulation of ''Super Intelligence'' - or AI - at the APEC summit in Shenzhen ahead of his meeting…
